source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Read and understand all test results. If there is a violation, always start with the result with the lowest amount of acceptable chlorine (mg/L). That is where your violation will follow.

6. Work with your team to set up a retest to check the level at different times of the day (such as the hot afternoon).
If the levels are routinely below your target level, have your team take every sample over the course of several days until the system is back up to standard.
3. Notify all affected parties with a “Boil Water Notice” that must contain this line: “You may want to carry out other precautions appropriate to your particular needs, such as seeking advice from your physician or giving your pharmacist more frequent cleaning.”

4. Work with your team to decide if and where you need to place new or additional valves or connections, such as pressure-relief valves; booster pumps; and/or backflow prevention devices.
